capacity.title: A 240-minute window becomes a feasible plan
capacity.summary: Subtract the scenario’s essential commitments before allocating study outcomes. The three allocations total the remaining 150 minutes.

nodes.label: 240 minutes initially available
nodes.description: The learner has a four-hour window before adding travel, a meal and a necessary transition.

nodes.label: 90 minutes essential
nodes.description: Reserve 45 minutes for the journey, 30 for a meal and 15 for transition: 45 + 30 + 15 = 90.

nodes.label: 150 minutes usable
nodes.description: Subtract essentials from the window: 240 − 90 = 150 minutes. This is a local scenario, not a universal capacity formula.

nodes.label: 90-minute checked draft
nodes.description: Allocate 90 minutes to drafting and checking the essential section; define the accepted state before starting.

nodes.label: 30-minute practice
nodes.description: Choose a bounded exercise that fits 30 minutes rather than an entire unestimated chapter.

nodes.label: 30-minute uncertainty reserve
nodes.description: Leave 30 minutes uncommitted for variation. The plan uses 90 + 30 + 30 = 150 minutes without reducing essential commitments.

attention-context.title: Leave and recover a specific working state
attention-context.summary: An urgent interruption requires a reachable response. A return cue preserves the next unfinished check; optional alerts can wait.

nodes.label: Draft in progress
nodes.description: The learner is checking a paragraph against its source when a message arrives.

nodes.label: Urgent responsibility?
nodes.description: Use the previously agreed communication rule to distinguish a required response from an optional alert.

nodes.label: Leave return cue
nodes.description: Record the current file, last verified sentence and next source check before switching when circumstances allow.

nodes.label: Respond to urgent input
nodes.description: Address the necessary call or message; record its actual duration rather than assuming every interruption has the same cost.

nodes.label: Resume named check
nodes.description: Read the cue, inspect the file for changes and restart at the recorded unfinished check. Record reconstruction time separately.

nodes.label: Queue optional alert
nodes.description: Leave the optional message for the agreed checking window and continue the current paragraph.

estimate.title: Ground a draft forecast in comparable work
estimate.summary: The supplied drafts took 70, 90 and 110 minutes. Preserve that variation and revise the comparison when inputs or review requirements differ.

nodes.label: Three completed drafts
nodes.description: Collect the observed 70-, 90- and 110-minute durations using the same completion definition.

nodes.label: Comparable new draft?
nodes.description: Check source familiarity, length and review scope. Similar-looking titles alone do not establish comparable work.

nodes.label: Provisional 70–110 range
nodes.description: Use the observed range as a planning starting point. Three examples do not establish a reliable percentile or confidence interval.

nodes.label: Identify relevant differences
nodes.description: If the new draft needs unfamiliar sources or extra review, name that added work and seek a closer comparator.

nodes.label: Reserve a realistic window
nodes.description: Choose a feasible window and review allowance. If a 40-minute promise cannot fit the evidence, reduce scope or renegotiate rather than hiding variation.

experiment.title: A four-session message-batching trial
experiment.summary: Compare two ordinary and two batching sessions with similar tasks, checked output and errors. Small samples support a reversible local choice.

nodes.label: Question and measures
nodes.description: Ask whether optional message batching helps checked drafting. Define checked paragraphs, errors, urgent interruptions and administration effort before trial results.

nodes.label: Two ordinary sessions
nodes.description: Observe two sessions with the learner’s usual message handling, keeping the focus window and draft size reasonably similar.

nodes.label: Two batching sessions
nodes.description: Observe two sessions with optional messages checked at the end while the agreed urgent route remains available.

nodes.label: Compare outcomes and context
nodes.description: Compare checked output and errors, not just attempts. Record workload, task difficulty and disruption differences that may explain results.

nodes.label: Keep, adjust or repeat
nodes.description: Choose a provisional routine if the benefit exceeds its cost; repeat a more comparable trial if the result is ambiguous. Do not claim universal causation.

weekly-review.title: Turn a backlog into a feasible week
weekly-review.summary: Two available windows cannot absorb every carried and newly proposed item. Keep, clarify, defer or renegotiate each commitment explicitly.

nodes.label: Collect seven unresolved options
nodes.description: Archive the two finished items; bring together three carried commitments and four new proposals without silently accepting all of them.

nodes.label: Check two available windows
nodes.description: Inspect essential commitments, needed inputs and the actual shape of the two remaining work windows.

nodes.label: Select two fitting outcomes
nodes.description: Choose two outcomes with checkable finish states and meaningful delay consequences that fit the available windows.

nodes.label: Defer or renegotiate others
nodes.description: Record which items are deferred, declined or reduced. Notify an affected promise holder through an authorized channel when a changed commitment requires it.

nodes.label: Review actual use next week
nodes.description: Compare finished outcomes, duration and changed constraints. Use the results to revise estimates rather than copy every unfinished item forward.
